weather.title: Ogden Valley weather: week of Nov. 9
weather.summary: A dry, mild week is forecast for Eden, Liberty and Huntsville. Highs of 59–63°, sunny to partly sunny all week. Lows of 33–36°, with Tuesday and Wednesday nights dropping to about 33°, near freezing. No rain or snow is forecast Monday through Saturday. Next weekend, a cooler, wetter turn is possible. On the colder nights, disconnect garden hoses and cover tender plants. It's a good week to finish fall yard work and get snow tires and winter gear ready.
weather.alt: Ben's Weather Desk, week of Nov. 9: Ben the moose at the news desk, with the 7-day forecast below: dry Monday through Thursday, highs 58 to 63, lows 33 to 36, a small rain chance Friday and Saturday and 36% Sunday.
weather.source: National Weather Service forecast for the Eden, Liberty and Huntsville area, issued 11:31 a.m. MST Nov. 8, 2026

weather.title: Ogden Valley weather: Nov. 6 to 11
weather.summary: A dry, sunny week: sunny to mostly sunny every day through Thursday, highs of 53–62°, no rain or snow in the forecast and calm wind. Frosty mornings with lows of 31–36°, coldest Friday night near 31°, so leave time to scrape the windshield. One lane of SR-39 in upper Ogden Canyon stays closed through April, with flaggers by day and a signal at night. Veterans Day, Wednesday, Nov. 11: sunny, high near 61°. A good week to finish yard cleanup, blow out sprinklers and put hoses away.
weather.alt: Ogden Valley weather briefing for Nov. 6 to 11: a six-day forecast, all sunny and dry, plus boxes on a dry sunny week, frosty mornings, the Ogden Canyon lane closure, Veterans Day, and a good-week-to list.
weather.source: National Weather Service point forecast for the Eden, Liberty and Huntsville area, issued 11:31 a.m. Nov. 6, 2026; UDOT Traffic (SR-39)

weather.title: Ogden Valley weather: Nov. 1 to 6
weather.summary: A soaking Sunday: rain turning to showers and thunderstorms (100%), with about three-quarters of an inch to an inch of rain possible and a high near 50°. A chance of light rain Monday through Wednesday (36–44%), then drier and sunnier by Thursday. Lows of 29–32° Monday through Friday nights, so cover tender plants and unhook hoses. Snow level near 6,600 feet, so the peaks may turn white while the Valley floor stays rain. Starting as early as Monday, Nov. 2, and through April, one lane of SR-39 in upper Ogden Canyon is closed, with alternating traffic around the clock. Air quality is Good.
weather.alt: Ogden Valley weather briefing for Nov. 1 to 6: a six-day forecast with Sunday highlighted at 100 percent, plus boxes on a soaking Sunday, frosty nights, snow up high, the Ogden Canyon lane closure, and a get-ready list.
weather.source: National Weather Service point forecast for the Eden, Liberty and Huntsville area, issued 12:31 a.m. Nov. 1, 2026; UDOT Traffic (SR-39); Utah Division of Air Quality forecast, issued 7:32 p.m. Oct. 31

weather.title: Ogden Valley weather: Oct. 29 to Nov. 4
weather.summary: Dry and mild today and early Friday, highs near 61°. Rain chances start Friday afternoon and evening (52%). Halloween looks wet: light rain Saturday turning to showers and thunderstorms by evening (99%), highs near 58°, so plan trick-or-treating with rain gear. Sunday, Nov. 1, brings showers and thunderstorms, then rain and snow likely Sunday night, with a chance of rain and snow Monday morning; lows near 29–31°. Snow level near 8,000 feet. Mostly sunny Tuesday and Wednesday, highs in the 50s. Air quality is Good. Clocks fall back one hour early Sunday, Nov. 1.
weather.alt: Ogden Valley weather briefing for Oct. 29 to Nov. 4: a six-day forecast with Saturday and Sunday highlighted at 99 percent, plus boxes on a wet Halloween, rain and snow Sunday night, clocks falling back, and drying out, and a get-ready list.

featured.title: Valley Time Capsule: What's under Pineview?
featured.line: About 1920, water bubbled up out of the ground on its own at "Artesian Park" near Huntsville. Today it's under Pineview Reservoir. Kids can ride our new Time Train through Valley history on the Utah Depot page. Photo: Fred Pack, about 1920, J. Willard Marriott Library, University of Utah.
